summary: The study investigates the reversibility of elementary mechanisms in atomic-layer epitaxy (ALE) and sublimation of (001) CdTe. It shows that the sublimation process involves mechanisms opposite to those in ALE growth, with distinct surface reconstructions and kinetics. The growth and sublimation processes are analyzed using reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED), revealing the formation of different surface types and the role of Cd and Te atoms in surface reconstructions.
evidence: The experiments were performed in a MBE system equipped with Cd, Te, and CdTe cells. The ALE and sublimation mechanisms are studied by using a reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) system operating at 30 kV. The results concern the time variations of the intensity of the specular spot recorded with a charge-coupled-device camera. ALE growth of CdTe was performed at a substrate temperature of 290 °C. The key point is that in all these cases the sequence of the surfaces formed during the sublimation process is in agreement with a mechanism which is the opposite of the mechanism previously described for ALE growth.
